Generate alt text for a micropubr figure

Source: R/mp_methods.R
mp_alt_text.Rd

Describes a figure for readers who cannot see it: the chart type, what is plotted against what, how it is grouped, how much data it shows, the key result (e.g. which group has the highest diversity, how many taxa are differentially abundant) and the statistics in its subtitle and caption. Journals increasingly ask for alt text with every figure.

Usage

mp_alt_text(plot)

Arguments

plot

A figure made by an mp_*() function (any ggplot works, with a more generic description).

Value

A character string.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
p <- mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",
              test = "kruskal")
#> Warning: Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = 3), Mock (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil (n = 3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have little power and their p-values are unstable at this size.
mp_alt_text(p)
#> [1] "Box plots of Shannon, coloured by SampleType (9 categories), based on 26 data rows. Median Shannon is highest in Soil (6.58) and lowest in Tongue (3.29). Statistics: Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.005."
# }
